title: VecFlow SDK: cross-lang streaming adapters and retry ergonomics for vectors + reranker
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement a cross-language set of ergonomic streaming adapters and retry profiles for vector (embeddings) and reranking endpoints. Deliverables: idiomatic streaming helper in Python/TS/Go, a resumable cursor abstraction, configurable backpressure profiles, and documentation + examples that show cost/latency trade-offs. Goal is API parity across SDKs while allowing language-specific ergonomics.
acceptance_criteria: Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs each expose a streaming adapter with the same high-level surface (StartStream, NextBatch, ResumeCursor)
Adapters include built-in retry/backoff profiles that match platform SLOs and can be overridden per-call
Pagination/batching helper supports windowed merges and configurable max_token_batch and max_item_batch
Examples (one per language) demonstrate: long-run streaming with intermittent failures, resumable pagination after client disconnect, and client-side backpressure control
Unit + integration tests covering retry jitter/backoff, KV cache prefix reuse, and end-to-end reranker rerank-stream correctness
API docs and migration guide for existing iterator helpers published in the SDK repo and Redwood docs
design_notes: Use a small 'VecFlow' abstraction that separates transport (HTTP/GRPC) from streaming strategy (windowed, continuous, resumable)
Retry profiles: fast-fail for single-token echo errors; exponential backoff with jitter for connectivity; a bounded retry budget tied to request timeout
ResumeCursor will encode: model, route, last_seq_token, and optional client-side metadata; avoid embedding raw user data
Client ergonomics: Python async iterator, TS async generator, Go channel-based streamer; surface a unified semantic in docs while keeping language idioms
Batching heuristics: prefer size-limited batches (max_items) with timeout flush; allow explicit flush() for synchronous UX
Backpressure: expose a token_budget knob and a pause/resume signal for applications with variable downstream consumers
tasks: Spec: finalize VecFlow abstraction and examples (engineering + DX)
Implement Python async iterator and retry profiles
Implement TypeScript async generator and streaming helpers
Implement Go channel-based streamer and resumable cursor helper
Add unit/integration tests and flaky-run harness for intermittent network failures
Write cross-sdk examples: long-running rerank stream, incremental embeddings uploader + pagination
Doc: API reference, migration guide, and cost/latency benchmark snippets
Release: coordinate with runtime team to add server-side resume tokens and small compatibility patch
